verdict.rationale: GitLab combines source control and CI/CD in one platform, and automations are defined in a project CI/CD configuration file. That implies they can be versioned in the repo and reviewed through merge requests, and agent actions are logged in an audit trail. The evidence never explicitly describes versioning, reviewing, or rolling back the automations themselves. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that pipeline/automation definitions are versioned and reviewed via merge requests, any documented rollback or revert of automations, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: Planning, source control, and CI/CD in one platform.
editing your project’s GitLab CI/CD configuration file
turning issues into merge requests, remediating vulnerabilities, and reviewing code
Every agent action shows up in the audit trail.
